entities.summary: Claudius Clavus (Suartho), also known as Nicholas Niger, was a Danish geographer and cartographer who is sometimes considered to be the first Nordic cartographer. Born in Denmark around 1450, Clavus spent much of his life studying the ancient Greeks and their geography. His most famous work, the Suartho Atlas, a collection of maps and descriptions of the world as known to the ancient Greeks, was completed in the late 15th century and provided a crucial source of information for later cartographers. The atlas includes maps of the Mediterranean region, the Black Sea, and the Baltic Sea, and provides detailed descriptions of the geography, climate, and cultures of the regions it covers. Clavus's work had a significant impact on the development of cartography in Europe, and his maps and descriptions of the world were studied and used by cartographers for centuries. He is also known for his work on the geography of Scandinavia and his contributions to the understanding of the region's natural resources.
